name: AI Literature and Research Assistants
blurb: Tools that search, summarise and extract data from scientific papers.
title: AI Literature and Research Assistants
answer: AI research assistants find and summarise papers and pull structured data from them for evidence synthesis. Accuracy on extraction can be high in controlled tests, one study found a large language model extracted 160 clinical trial data points with 96.3 percent accuracy, but omissions and hallucinated details remain, so outputs need checking.

reading.body:
AI literature assistants can extract structured data from papers at high accuracy in controlled tests, but every extracted number still needs checking against the source.

The one measured result here is a proof of concept: a large language model pulled 160 clinical trial data points at 96.3 percent accuracy. That is a single study on a bounded extraction task, not a general accuracy rate for the category. The stated failure modes are omissions and hallucinated details, which are the errors that survive a spot check because the output looks complete.

For AI in drug discovery, the value is triage at the front of the pipeline, finding and summarising papers before a human reads them. The risk sits at the back, where an extracted number enters an analysis and is treated as read from the paper. The working rule the data supports is to use these tools to find and triage, then verify each number against the paper.

Nothing here covers cost, throughput, or how accuracy holds on tables, figures, or supplements rather than trial text. It also says nothing about compute, buildings, or power, so no claim about the infrastructure behind these tools can be drawn from it.

sections.body: Use these tools to find and triage, then verify every extracted number against the paper before it enters an analysis.
